The '''National Statistics Office''' ({{langx|ne|राष्ट्रिय तथ्याङ्क कार्यालय}}) formerly known as '''Central Bureau of Statistics''' ({{Langx|ne|केन्द्रीय तथ्याङ्क विभाग}}), is the central agency for the collection, consolidation, processing, analysis, publication and dissemination of statistics in [[Nepal]]. The Office is under the [[Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Introduction |url=https://nsonepal.gov.np/pages/76831566/ |website=National Statistics Office}}</ref> One of its core tasks is to research and publish censuses of Nepal, the most prominent one being the overall [[Census in Nepal|population census]] and [[Demographics of Nepal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ekantipur.com/2012/11/26/top-story/census-puts-nepals-population-at-26.49-million/363244.html |title=Census puts Nepal's population at 26.49 million |publisher=[[Kantipur (daily)]] |access-date=26 November 2013 |archive-date=29 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121129100125/http://www.ekantipur.com/2012/11/26/top-story/census-puts-nepals-population-at-26.49-million/363244.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==History==
The Central Bureau of Statistics was established on 1 January 1959 as per the Statistics Act, 2015 B.S (1958 A.D). It replaced the former '''Department of Statistics''' ({{Langx|ne|संख्या विभाग}}) established in 1950.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://nepal.unfpa.org/sites/default/files/pub-pdf/PopulationMonograph2014Volume1.pdf |title=POPULATION MONOGRAPH OF NEPAL VOLUME I (Population Dynamics) |publisher=Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS), Nepal |year=2014}}</ref> The Bureau was initially under the [[Ministry of Finance (Nepal)|Ministry of Finance]] and later moved under the [[National Planning Commission of Nepal]], which is headed by the [[Prime Minister of Nepal]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Introduction & History|url=http://www.npc.gov.np/en/page/2/about_us/introduction_history|publisher=National Planning Commission|access-date=20 October 2017|archive-date=2 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171102170521/http://www.npc.gov.np/en/page/2/about_us/introduction_history|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

After the [[April 2015 Nepal earthquake]], the Bureau, in coordination with the [[United Nations]], collected data regarding the damages in order for the [[Government of Nepal]] to support and compensate the victims.<ref>{{cite web|title=CBS collecting details of loss in 14 quake-hit districts afresh|date=17 January 2016|url=https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/nepal-earthquake-cbs-collecting-details-of-loss-in-14-quake-hit-districts-afresh/|publisher=The Himalayan Times|access-date=20 October 2017|archive-date=29 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029013435/https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/nepal-earthquake-cbs-collecting-details-of-loss-in-14-quake-hit-districts-afresh/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=CBS to submit data on quake survivors soon|date=19 December 2015|url=https://thehimalayantimes.com/business/cbs-to-submit-data-on-quake-survivors-soon/|publisher=The Himalayan Times|access-date=20 October 2017|archive-date=29 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029012922/https://thehimalayantimes.com/business/cbs-to-submit-data-on-quake-survivors-soon/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Before 2015, different Nepalese governmental organisations gathered statistical information on their own. This led to inconsistencies in statistical information, for which the Bureau called for improvement of the processes, which, however, were not implemented as of 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=CBS launches Kathmandu Declaration|date=8 September 2015|url=https://thehimalayantimes.com/business/cbs-launches-kathmandu-declaration/|publisher=The Himalayan Times|access-date=20 October 2017|archive-date=29 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029013423/https://thehimalayantimes.com/business/cbs-launches-kathmandu-declaration/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 13 October 2022, the existing Central Bureau of Statistics was upgraded to National Statistics Office as per the new Statistics Act of 2079 B.S (2022 A.D) and brought under the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.<ref name=":0" />

The Office's main functions include providing its government with statistics to help with public policy planning, collecting and analyzing socioeconomic data, and developing methodologies for reliable data collection and implementation.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://cbs.gov.np/main-functions/ |title=Main Functions |access-date=30 January 2019 |archive-date=25 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190825204329/https://cbs.gov.np/main-functions/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
